# Jetpack Compose enhancement policy

`enhance-execute` owns workflow order and builds. This policy defines the final Compose shape. The generated Compose source is the authoritative UI specification; screenshots are independent render evidence. Preserve existing target behavior unless the file plan explicitly changes it.

## Read first

Use the completed planning artifacts:

- `.locofy/agent/memory/file-plan.md`
- `.locofy/agent/memory/state-variants.md`
- `.locofy/agent/memory/generated-component-groups.md`
- `<incoming>/.locofy/agent/memory/screenshot-mapping.md`

Apply those decisions directly. The bundled probes are the detailed executable specification; do not duplicate them with ad hoc scans.

## Render-equivalent architecture migration

All architecture gates remain mandatory. Satisfy them by moving and wiring generated UI, not by redesigning it.

- Re-read each original generated screen/component immediately before writing its final destination.
- Preserve the composable child tree and z-order, except duplicate overlays already painted inside a flattened bitmap (see visual translation).
- Preserve Compose modifier order. `padding().background()` is not interchangeable with `background().padding()`.
- Preserve exact layout APIs and semantics: `requiredSize`, `size`, `width`, `height`, `offset`, `wrapContentSize`, alignment, arrangements, clipping, scrolling, and overlays may not be substituted merely to make code cleaner, except for changes required by the shared **Design-optimisation exception set** in `enhance-execute` and the visual-translation rules below. That geometry set is exhaustive; do not infer additional responsive-layout exceptions.
- Preserve every numeric value exactly, including zeroes, negative values, fixed frame sizes, and long decimals, except when the shared Design-optimisation exception set requires removing a reference viewport width.
- Preserve borders, strokes, radii, shadows, typography metrics, colors, brushes, alpha, resources, content scale, and visible state defaults exactly. Translate CSS `shadow-[…]` as specified below; do not replace a hard offset slab with Material `Modifier.shadow` blur.
- Move navigation ownership into `MainScaffold` without adding Scaffold padding, system insets, or bar measurements that change the generated content coordinate system. Use Scaffold slots when they are render-equivalent; when generated chrome overlays content, keep it as a `MainScaffold`-owned overlay instead of forcing slot padding.
- Fix invalid generated Kotlin types or syntax without changing the represented visual value.

## HTML → Compose visual translation

- **Baked-in bitmap layers.** Open banner/hero/background drawables. If the bitmap already contains a logo or title, do not also compose that logo/title as a sibling `Image`/`Text`. Locofy often exports both the flattened PNG and the vector children; drawing both is a mismatch.
- **Do not clip chrome labels.** CSS overflow is visible; `Modifier.height` plus vertical padding squeezes `Text`. Icon+label cells (bottom nav) must show the full label: hug the column or `wrapContentHeight` the text. Do not render iOS `Home-indicator-bar` (or `ic_home_indicator*`) as Android chrome, and do not pad `MainScaffold` for that extra height.
- **Negative spacing is layout, not offset.** Tailwind `mt-[-Npx]` / negative `gap` collapses layout (avatar overlapping a banner, then body text). `Modifier.offset` does not. Use `Arrangement.spacedBy((-N).dp)` or other layout-affecting spacing so text under the overlap matches the screenshot.
- **Shadows.** `shadow-[0px_Ypx_0px_#RRGGBB]` is a hard Y-dp color slab under the fill (`offset` / `drawBehind`), not `Modifier.shadow`. `shadow-[0px_Ypx_Bpx_rgba(…)]` is a soft shadow — match offset, blur, and color. A missing Tailwind shadow on a primary button, FAB, sheet, or card is a fail.
- **Stretch vs pack.** Parent `items-end` plus child `self-stretch` is fill-width; then honor the child's `justify-center`. Do not shrink a stretched tertiary action (“Clear all”) into end-aligned packed text under a full-width primary button.
- **Control glyphs.** Checkbox/radio ticks are centered in a CSS `box-border` frame (24dp box, 2dp border → 20dp inner). Apply the inner `<img>` insets from HTML; do not Fit-scale the raw SVG in a nested Icon helper so the tick sits in a corner.

Do not infer dimensions from the screenshot when the generated source provides them. Do not replace source values with conventional design-system values. Do not discard “frame-coordinate junk”: if generated production UI references it, it is required. Any intentional visual delta needs explicit user approval. The baked-in bitmap and iOS home-indicator rules above are screenshot-true corrections, not optional redesigns.

## Feature contract

Give every destination one feature directory and this complete set:

```text
ui/search/
  SearchKey.kt
  SearchState.kt
  SearchAction.kt
  SearchEvent.kt
  SearchViewModel.kt
  SearchRoot.kt
  SearchScreen.kt
  SearchScreenPreview.kt
  model/SortMode.kt
util/FlowExt.kt
theme/{Color,Typography,Dimens,Theme}.kt
MainScaffold.kt
component/bottomNavigationBar/BottomNavigationBar.kt
component/bottomNavItem/BottomNavItem.kt
```

- `Key`: `@Serializable data object SearchKey : NavKey`.
- `State`: one `@Serializable data class` with empty or neutral defaults. Put each supporting enum, sealed type, and model in its own `model/*.kt` file.
- `Action`: state-changing user intents.
- `Event`: navigation and one-shot effects.
- `ViewModel`: constructor-injected dependencies, `MutableStateFlow`, and `Channel<Event>`. Load preset data in `init`, not in State defaults.
- `Root`: obtains the ViewModel, uses `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()` and `collectAsEffect`, and forwards navigation.
- `Screen`: pure `(state, onAction, modifier) -> Unit` UI with no ViewModel or backstack reference.
- `ScreenPreview`: the only screen file containing `@Preview`; wrap the Screen in `AppTheme`.

Keep every Action/Event case live. Model navigation as an Event:

```kotlin
Screen action -> ViewModel sends Event.Navigate(key) -> Root forwards it -> backStack.add(key)
```

Represent screenshots of the same destination with state fields and conditional UI in one feature. For example, `isFilterVisible`, `selectedSegment`, and `loadState` belong in `SearchState`; matching Actions update them. Keep separate routes only for separate destinations.

Annotate State, NavKeys, and feature models with `@Serializable`. Prefer serializable domain values such as `String` for dates; use `@Transient` with a default only for a genuinely non-serializable State field.

Define `collectAsEffect` once in `util/FlowExt.kt`.

## Files and components

- Do not create `ui/{feature}/composable/`, `ui/{feature}/composables/`, or feature-local `component(s)/` directories.
- Keep screen UI inline unless it is a component in `generated-component-groups.md`.
- Ignore file length, repetition, and visual similarity when deciding component boundaries.
- Put every canonical generated component in `component/{camelCaseComponentName}/{Name}.kt`, for example `component/datePicker/DatePicker.kt`. Component folder names must be lower camelCase; kebab-case, snake_case, and PascalCase folders are invalid.
- In empty-copy mode, files already staged together under `component/{camelCaseComponentName}/` are generated siblings, not existing target matches. Consolidate every sibling into the single group canonical and preserve an explicit typed case/caller mapping for each raw member.
- Create one canonical component for every row in `generated-component-groups.md`, including one-caller rows. Strip terminal digits from type/function/file names (`Button1`, `Button2` → `Button`), rewrite all callers, and remove superseded declarations.
- Preserve an existing canonical component's behavior, API, and callers. Generalize it only for cases recorded in its generated group.
- Put nav chrome in the common component layout: `component/bottomNavigationBar/BottomNavigationBar.kt`, `component/bottomNavItem/BottomNavItem.kt`, and `component/appTopBar/AppTopBar.kt` when a top bar is needed.
- Put repositories beside their feature in `ui/{feature}/repository/`, with interface and implementation in separate files. Add them only for real data access.
- Keep one top-level `*Screen.kt` per feature. A second destination gets its own feature; screen-only child UI remains inline in that screen.
- Treat input affordances as editable values unless their recorded interaction contract is read-only. Use value/onValueChange pairs for editable values, typed configuration for caller-selectable related states, and callbacks for caller-owned actions. Group related visibility controls into typed cases that render their selected region. Apply each declared prop/state in rendering or interaction and keep outer positioning in the caller.

Preserve design-authored identifiers exactly:

```kotlin
// Figma variable
val bgPrim = ...

// Component state
val selectedDate7 = ...
```

Keep both the marker and identifier through moves and canonicalization. Use semantic names only for new, unmarked tokens and types.

## Theme, resources, and Compose quality

- Migrate all generated `DesignTokens` values referenced by production UI into `theme/{Color,Typography,Dimens,Theme}.kt` one-for-one, update callers to `CustomTheme`, then delete `DesignTokens.kt`. Keep each referenced generated token name as an exact-value theme field or alias so its provenance remains mechanically verifiable.
- Define `CustomColors`, `CustomTypography`, and `CustomDimensions` as `@Immutable` data classes backed by composition locals. Expose them through `CustomTheme`.
- Keep raw color values as top-level `internal val` declarations in `Color.kt`; `CustomColors` is the public theme surface.
- Use `CustomTheme.dimens` for `dp`/`sp`, `CustomTheme.typography` for complete `TextStyle`s, and `CustomTheme.colors` for UI colors. Set `Text` with `style = ...` and the required color; keep font properties inside the style.
- Semantic roles may alias generated tokens, but may not round, merge, reinterpret, or replace their values. If the source uses both `132.dp` and `132.0001.dp`, preserve both.
- Put user-visible text and accessibility descriptions in `strings.xml`, resolved with `stringResource`. Use the incoming drawable assets through `painterResource`.
- Use Material3 components and `HorizontalDivider`.
- Hoist `rememberScrollState()` and `rememberLazyListState()` to named values.
- Use `Modifier.weight()` from a Row/Column scope. A Modifier extension that reads composition locals is `@Composable`; a pure extension accepts resolved values as parameters.
- Set `Box.contentAlignment` when the Box has child content to align.
- Import only referenced symbols. Plain State/Action/Event/Key/model files have no Compose runtime or UI imports; use either a wildcard or specific imports, not both.
- Keep persistent domain models free of Android resource IDs. Transient Event payloads may use `@StringRes`; navigation enums use the resource IDs described below.

## Nav3 and bottom tabs

Use Navigation3 `1.0.1` and `androidx.navigation3.runtime.NavKey`. Apply the Kotlin serialization plugin and dependency.

Start the app with `setContent { AppTheme { MainScaffold() } }`.

```kotlin
val backStack = rememberNavBackStack(HomeKey)

NavDisplay(
    backStack = backStack,
    entryDecorators = listOf(
        rememberSaveableStateHolderNavEntryDecorator(),
        rememberViewModelStoreNavEntryDecorator(),
    ),
    entryProvider = entryProvider { /* entry<HomeKey> { ... } */ },
)
```

Use the no-argument saver form above and exactly those two decorators in that order. Derive the current route from `backStack.lastOrNull()`. Keep bars owned by `MainScaffold` and destination Screens content-only. Use `topBar`/`bottomBar` slots only when their measured padding matches the generated source; otherwise render the bars as `MainScaffold` overlays with the generated bounds and z-order.

Every `BottomNavItem` owns:

- a distinct `NavKey`;
- its own complete feature set and `entry<Key>` registration;
- a distinct localized placeholder when the real screen is absent;
- `@StringRes labelRes: Int` and `@DrawableRes iconRes: Int`.

Resolve labels with `stringResource(item.labelRes)` and icons with `painterResource(item.iconRes)`. Reuse the exact tab assets, labels, and selected/unselected colors recorded in `screenshot-mapping.md`. Show a back affordance for pushed destinations, not tab roots.

## Verification

For every canonical `Name.kt`, create sibling `NameColors.kt` with an `@Immutable` light-theme color set backed by `CustomTheme.colors`, and `NamePreview.kt` with `@Preview` coverage for its distinct generated Figma configurations. Use no-op callbacks or preview-local display state and add focused component tests when the target already has a component-test convention.

Use `references/architecture-pattern.md`, `references/nav3-navigation.md`, or `references/design-tokens.md` only when the current change needs a concrete implementation pattern. The rules above are authoritative.

From the target project root, run the bundled acceptance probe unchanged:

```bash
node <skill-dir>/references/acceptance-probes.cjs
```

Batch all reported fixes, then rerun. Completion requires exit 0 and the literal final line `PROBES_RESULT:ALL_PASS`.

When build verification is enabled, use the APK emitted by `enhance-execute` Step 7:

1. Launch it with `launch-emulator.cjs`. Use the selected Android emulator hardware profile with its status bar and camera cutout visible.
2. Read every reference screenshot at the exact generated-folder path from the kickoff prompt, then capture one uncropped, unmasked full-display emulator screenshot for every mapped design state with `capture-screenshot.cjs`. Do not search for alternate copies, and do not hide or normalize hardware-specific system regions.
3. Compare each design/capture pair and inspect the status-bar and camera-cutout regions. Any text or interactive control under, behind, or obscured by either region is a visual failure. Fix it and recapture; never waive an obstruction as an emulator or hardware difference.
4. Write `.locofy/agent/memory/visual-verification.md`. Record the selected emulator once as `DEVICE:<model>`. For every screen, record `STATUS_BAR:VISIBLE CAMERA_CUTOUT:VISIBLE SAFE_AREA:PASS` only after both regions are visible and clear of text and controls; record `SAFE_AREA:FAIL` for any overlap.
5. Run:

```bash
node <skill-dir>/references/visual-verify-probe.cjs \
  --screenshot-mapping "<incoming>/.locofy/agent/memory/screenshot-mapping.md"
```

The probe is a hard safe-area acceptance gate: missing per-screen evidence, hidden or cropped system UI, and every `SAFE_AREA:FAIL` block completion. A buildable project is complete at `VISUAL_RESULT:ALL_PASS`. If the APK cannot be built, record one `VISUAL_BLOCKED` report row, run the visual probe for its honest result, and report only the build blockage plus acceptance-probe status. When `skipBuild` is set, skip build-dependent visual work.
